title: Writ op envelope payload
description: The payload half of the op envelope: the canonical JSON blob stored at op.json in an op commit's tree. The other half of the envelope (op id, parent op ids, author, timestamp, signature) is carried by the commit itself and is not represented here. See spec/op-envelope.md for field semantics and spec/canonicalization.md for the byte encoding this blob must use. Unknown top-level fields are permitted: readers preserve and ignore fields they do not understand.

object_id.description: Identifier of the collaborative object this op belongs to. Opaque at this layer: printable non-space ASCII, no further structure imposed here. The workspace-global id format is specified separately (WRIT-16).

object_type.description: The collaborative object's type. `schema` is the one type this specification defines; every other value is declared by a schema object in the log, and is namespace-qualified as <namespace>.<type> (spec/schema-ops.md §2), each segment matching the bare form and its own 64-character bound, for 129 (64 + '.' + 64) total. Deliberately not an enum: readers must tolerate object types they do not know (preserve and ignore, never drop). This layer admits both the bare and qualified shapes and enforces nothing about which a given value must be; whether a non-schema object_type is required to be qualified is a schema-layer rule (spec/schema-ops.md §2) this envelope layer does not know or enforce.

op_type.description: The operation's type within its object type's vocabulary, e.g. create. Deliberately not an enum: the op types an object type admits are declared by a schema object in the log (spec/schema-ops.md), and readers must tolerate op types they do not know. Unlike object_type, op_type is never namespace-qualified: op types live inside a type's own vocabulary and were never globally contended, so they stay bare and 64 characters regardless of the qualified form object_type now admits.

op_version.description: Schema version of this op type's body, starting at 1. A small integer, always exactly representable as an IEEE-754 double; anything that could grow past 2^53 must be a string field instead (see spec/canonicalization.md on numbers).

body.description: Type-specific operation content. An open slot at this layer: the fields a (object_type, op_type, op_version) triple admits are declared by a schema object in the log (spec/schema-ops.md). Unknown body fields are likewise preserved and ignored.
